div.div: لَأّلٌ (Fr, S, K) and ↓ لَأّ=ءٌ and ↓ لَأْلَآءٌ , (K,) all contr. to analogy [if the radical letters be لألأ], and the last a strange form, mentioned by few authors, and disapproved by most: (TA:) the regular from would be لُؤْلُئِىٌّ; not لَأّ=ءٌ, as J asserts it to be, [unless the radical letters be لأأ], nor لَأّ=لٌ (K) [unless it be from a triliteral root, augmented, and thus rendered a quasi-quadriliteral-radical; (see a remark at the head of this art.; and see حَيَّةٌ;) in which case, either the added letter or the last radical letter may be omitted in the formation of this epithet]: (K:) A seller of pearls. (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
